class_name: 強調-比喩-トバカリニ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Describes a manner as though it were speech: the quoted words are usually not actually spoken but what the person's bearing broadcasts (待ってましたとばかりに, 早く行けとばかりに). It very often quotes an imperative or a set phrase (ここぞとばかりに, これでもかとばかりに), and it suits narration rather than casual talk. The close kin 〜んばかり attaches to a verb stem and says the action itself was on the brink, so it also covers non-speech verbs (泣かんばかり) where とばかりに cannot go.

examples.ruby: 待[ま]ってましたとばかりに、子供[こども]たちが庭[にわ]に飛[と]び出[だ]した。
examples.english: The kids burst out into the yard as if they'd been waiting for the word.

examples.ruby: 出番[でばん]だとばかりに、犬[いぬ]がリードをくわえて玄関[げんかん]に立[た]った。
examples.english: As if his moment had come, the dog stood at the door with his leash in his mouth.

examples.ruby: 早[はや]く行[い]けとばかりに、店長[てんちょう]が私[わたし]の背中[せなか]を押[お]した。
examples.english: The manager gave me a push in the back, as if to say get moving.
